g1_rf1#1.killer: Concentrator capacity for the refill the idea needs
g1_rf1#1.why: The capacity "freed" by Talnakh is already booked for Norilsk-1 at 7 Mtpa, so there is no new saving and only about 0.6 Mtpa is left for Maslovskoye's roughly 8 Mtpa.
g1_rf1#1.screen: 8 market/capacity: concentrator room for Norilsk-1 plus Maslovskoye 0.50 (room for Maslovskoye alone, after the planned Norilsk-1 feed, 0.07–0.28); 9 baseline: Nornickel's own plan is already this idea, ratio about 1.0; ceiling if all concentrator capital (about half of the 37%) is removed 1.23; 10 recovery: no ore-type recovery found for the Norilsk concentrator (silicate-bound Ni floats poorly), not scored

g1_rf2#1.killer: Metal loss XRT can afford on Norilsk-1 disseminated ore
g1_rf2#1.why: Pairing the two steps is only a booking change, and a 1.09–1.16× grade gain on 40% of the cost gives at most 1.05×, while the loss XRT can afford is below the best claim.
g1_rf2#1.screen: 10 recovery: metal loss XRT can afford vs claimed loss 0.35–0.65; 9 baseline: ratio 1.03–1.05 for a feed-grade gain of 1.094–1.156× at 98% recovery, applied to processing plus concentrator capital (40.5% of cost); 8 capacity: same Norilsk concentrator room as Idea 1, 0.50; 13 pilot proof: only an unaudited release from another ore (Selebi), not scored

g1_neg#2.killer: Availability gain needed for a 1.5× cost cut
g1_neg#2.why: Each availability point adds about 1% of output, so the few points available give at most 1.04× and cannot stand in for a capacity stage.
g1_neg#2.screen: 9 baseline: ratio 1.02 for +2 points and 1.04 for +5 points (80% of cost fixed); 8 scale: availability gain needed to stand in for the +8 Mtpa stage 0.06; 13 pilot proof: measuring a 2–5 point gain needs many months per arm, not scored

g1_rf1#3.killer: Serious failures to show the register halves the collapse rate (Poisson, 80% power, 2:1 split)
g1_rf1#3.why: Cutting the median repair time from 30 to 6 months is right on safety and compliance grounds, but the losses it targets are about 3–4% of full cost, so the ratio stays under 1.1 and the benefit cannot be shown statistically.
g1_rf1#3.screen: 9 baseline: ceiling ratio 1.03–1.04 even if all foundation losses (2%) plus one Ambarnaya-scale claim ($1.74bn) every 10–20 years were removed, against about $8.1bn a year of cash opex plus capex; 13 pilot proof: events seen vs events needed to show the collapse rate halved 0.035; 4 frozen-ground strength: not decisive, since the register changes no design
